messages:
Sam (CS): Heads up — a customer reported an uptick in confidently wrong regulatory statements after last night's rollout. Pasting excerpts below.
Sam (CS): Customer prompt (redacted): "Summarize compliance obligations for Acme's EU payroll processing."
Sam (CS): Model response (excerpt): "You must register under EU Payroll Directive 4.3 and submit annex B to the Commission by April 1st." Customer says there is no such directive — this is fabricated.
Sam (CS): Issue started ~2026-03-16 23:40 UTC, matching canary->prod promotion.
ops-bot: Deployment 'fastpath-opt-4' promoted to prod at 2026-03-16T23:35:12Z by deployer.
Matt (Eng): Thanks, Sam. Can you attach the full request payload and the model id/variant from the request headers?
Sam (CS): Request id=req_0a7f1c, model=redwood-small-v1.8-q4-fastpath (per headers). Payload (redacted): {"input":"Summarize compliance obligations for EU payroll processing"}.
Jordan (Repro): I can repro locally with that model id. On quick look prefix cache seems to return a stale continuation when the token sequence includes 'EU payroll' — cache key tweak in fastpath-opt-4 may be too aggressive.
Elaine (Ops): If prefix cache keying is wrong, we should rollback fastpath-opt-4 on prod now. Any quick mitigations besides rollback?
Matt (Eng): Temporary mitigation: disable prefix caching for redwood-small-v1.8-q4-fastpath for high-sensitivity routes (customer-success, finance customers) and reduce A/B exposure to <5%.
Jordan (Repro): Repro steps I ran:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDSK" -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1.8-q4-fastpath","input":"Summarize compliance obligations for EU payroll processing"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response returned an asserted directive. Running same prompt against redwood-small-v1.7 returns a cautious, non-assertive answer with correct references.
Sam (CS): Customer asking for rollback ETA and root cause. They've stopped sending traffic for now but want confirmation.
ops-bot: Rollback job scheduled. Initiating rollback of 'fastpath-opt-4' at 2026-03-16T23:50:10Z. change_id=chg_98765.
Matt (Eng): I'll grab KV cache traces and cache hit keys for req_0a7f1c and nearby ids. Need to see if cached continuation included hallucinated tokens.
Jordan (Repro): Also flagging quantized execution path: fastpath changes route some requests to a newer quantized kernel that may behave slightly differently on logits for token positions ~12-18. Would like logits trace for those tokens.
Elaine (Ops): Rollback in progress. Notifying customers in the incident banner.
ops-bot: Rollback completed 2026-03-16T23:59:10Z change_id=chg_98765 status=success.
Jordan (Repro): Quick A/B after rollback: v1.7 (baseline) vs v1.8-q4-fastpath (pre-rollback) — baseline hedges and cites, fastpath asserted a specific nonexistent directive. Post-rollback traffic to baseline shows expected output.
Sam (CS): Customer confirmed in their sandbox the incorrect assertive claim is gone. They've asked for a postmortem and mitigation plan.
Matt (Eng): Filing P1 postmortem and RCA ticket: https://pm.redwood/INC-12345. Immediate next steps: revert cache-key change out of fastpath, add unit tests around token boundary caching, and log cached continuations for 48h.
Jordan (Repro): I'll produce a minimal automated reproducer that runs against variants and captures logits + cache hit traces, will attach results here.
Sam (CS): I'll collate the customer's full transcript and attach when they send it. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Elaine (Ops): Marking this incident resolved for now; follow-up in postmortem.
Matt (Eng): Agree — once postmortem lands we'll schedule a follow-up doc for safe rollout checklist for cache/key changes.
Sam (CS): Closing loop with customer and adding them to the PMR for timeline.
